key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with the best tribological performance at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the spray gas ratio could improve the durability of titanium implants exposed to friction in physiological environments.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Analyze coating phases using X-ray diffraction.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved wear resistance versus uncoated titanium and the lowest wear volumes at gas ratios of 3.0 and 3.3, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Tribological testing in Ringer’s solution does not establish long-term implant durability or in vivo osseointegration.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
